title: Intuit finds a buyer for Mailchimp in Bending Spoons
content:
Italian holding company Bending Spoons is acquiring marketing automation platform Mailchimp from Intuit, the companies announced Thursday.
As MarTech reported in the spring when layoffs at Mailchimp were announced, Intuit was essentially running the business for the cash flow but had no plans to grow Mailchimp or its product.
While Intuit’s desire to unload Mailchimp was not a surprise, the return on its investment surely is. Bending Spoons is paying $3.68 billion for Mailchimp, which is less than one-third of the $12 billion Intuit paid to buy the company in 2021.
This is familiar territory for Milan, Italy-based Bending Spoons, which scoops up distressed software assets. Mailchimp will join a portfolio that includes Airtable, AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Miro, Tractive, Vimeo, and WeTransfer. As an example, Bending Spoons paid $1.285 billion for Airtable, which was once valued at $11.7 billion at its peak.
In connection with the all-cash transaction, Intuit will invest $368 million of its proceeds into newly issued Bending Spoons equity. The acquisition, including the investment, is subject to customary closing conditions, such as regulatory approvals.

Mike Pastore is the Head of Content & Media at Third Door Media, the publisher of the Martech and Search Engine Land websites and the producer of the SMX and MarTech Conferences. In nearly three decades in B2B marketing, Mike has worked as an editor, writer, and marketer. He first wrote about marketing in 1998 for internet.com (later Jupitermedia). He then worked with marketers at some of the best-known brands in B2B tech, creating content for marketing campaigns at both Jupitermedia and QuinStreet. Prior to joining Third Door Media as the Editorial Director of the MarTech website, he led demand generation at B2B media company TechnologyAdvice.
